phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The main NLTS-type lower bound is stated quantitatively in the theorem.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: There exists a family of Z2-symmetric local Hamiltonians H_n such that every Z2-symmetric depth-d circuit applied to a Z2-symmetric product state has energy greater than epsilon*n once n is sufficiently large.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Verify the theorem statement or its finite-instance quantitative projections from the packaged derivation/evidence.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The paper gives an explicit QAOA approximation-ratio upper bound on bipartite D-regular graphs.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For bipartite D-regular graphs, the level-p QAOA approximation ratio is bounded above by 5/6 + sqrt(D-1)/(3D) in the stated depth regime.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Evaluate or verify the approximation-ratio bound and its depth condition for the claimed graph family.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The 1D ring-of-disagrees setting yields explicit approximation-ratio limitations for shallow symmetric circuits and QAOA.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For the 1D ring-of-disagrees problem, shallow symmetric circuits and QAOA obey the stated nontrivial approximation-ratio upper bounds.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Check the analytical or numerical approximation-ratio bounds for the stated 1D benchmark.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Approximation ratios of level-1 QAOA and RQAOA are plotted for 16 random 3-regular Ising instances with n = 32.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For n = 32 random 3-regular Ising instances, the reported RQAOA approximation ratios improve on the corresponding level-1 QAOA ratios in the plotted comparison.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Reproduce the n = 32 approximation-ratio comparison between level-1 QAOA and RQAOA on the stated instance family.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The same approximation-ratio comparison is shown for n = 100.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: For n = 100 random 3-regular Ising instances, the reported RQAOA approximation ratios improve on the corresponding level-1 QAOA ratios in the plotted comparison.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Reproduce the n = 100 approximation-ratio comparison between level-1 QAOA and RQAOA on the stated instance family.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Pseudocode for the recursive QAOA algorithm is presented.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The RQAOA algorithm iteratively eliminates variables until a residual nc-variable problem is solved classically.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Algorithm schematic/pseudocode only; no standalone quantitative verdict required.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The paper claims that the reduced problem preserves the constrained optimum and can be lifted back through xi.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: The variable-elimination step produces a reduced cost function whose optimum matches the constrained optimum of the original problem and can be lifted back via the map xi.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Verify the algebraic reduction and reconstruction map for the stated elimination step.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Classical simulability subsection and Lemma QAOAlevel1 around Eq. (isingcostfct)
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The paper provides analytic formulas for level-1 QAOA Ising correlators and claims efficient classical evaluation.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Level-1 RQAOA for Ising models can use analytically computable QAOA correlators, enabling efficient classical evaluation of the elimination rule.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Re-derive or evaluate the stated level-1 Ising correlator formulas and their computational scaling.

phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The paper contrasts QAOA with local classical algorithms on a family of 1D Ising instances.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: There exists a size-2^(n/3) family of 1D Ising instances where QAOA is bounded by p/(p+1) while a 1-local uniform classical algorithm achieves the optimum.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Verify the stated family construction together with the QAOA upper bound and the classical optimum-achieving rule.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Lemma RQAOA and derivation around Eqs. (distijx), (variabletoeliminate), and (paritypreservation)
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The paper claims exact success of level-1 RQAOA on 1D Ising chains with +/-1 couplings.
phase1_inventory.paper_assertion: Level-1 RQAOA exactly solves any 1D Ising chain with couplings J_k in {+1,-1}, achieving approximation ratio 1 through the stated elimination sequence.
phase1_inventory.reproducible_object: Verify the elimination rule, preserved coupling parity, and exact optimality claim for the 1D +/-1 Ising family.
